name: Kangaroo
intro: A kangaroo is an animal that hops on its back legs. It lives in Australia.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A kangaroo has big, strong back legs.
It has small front legs.
It has a long, strong tail.
A big kangaroo can be taller than a grown-up.
A mother kangaroo has a pouch on her belly.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Big kangaroos live only in Australia.
They live in groups.
A group of kangaroos is called a mob.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Kangaroos eat plants.
They mostly eat grass.
They also eat small bushes called shrubs.
Red kangaroos can go a long time without water.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
A new joey is about as small as a grape.
It crawls into its mom's pouch all by itself.
It drinks milk and grows in the pouch.
It stays in the pouch for many months.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A kangaroo can jump as far as two cars parked in a row.
It can hop as fast as a car on a town street.
Its tail helps it balance when it jumps.
Kangaroos are good swimmers.
Kangaroos thump their feet to warn others of danger.

vocab.meaning: An animal mom that carries her baby in a pouch.
A pocket of skin on a mother's belly.
